name: Gordon Brown
role: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer (1997-2007) and Prime Minister (2007-2010); UN Special Envoy for Global Education
summary: Gordon Brown is a Labour moderniser who combined market economics and an independent central bank with larger spending on health, tax credits and international development. As Prime Minister he steered the 2008-09 bank rescues and a G20 stimulus, and since leaving office he has campaigned for stronger global institutions, child-poverty action and a reformed, more devolved United Kingdom that keeps Scotland in the Union.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 2022 Commission recommends a constitutional right to health care for all based on need, not ability to pay; as Chancellor he raised National Insurance in 2002 to fund NHS spending.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Commission calls the minimum wage one of Labour's greatest achievements and wants it to keep increasing the incomes of the poorest paid; it sets no 'substantial' rise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The report he chaired blames 'outdated neo-liberal economic dogma' and says leaving everything to the free market will not work; he still favours market economy with state support.

public-ownership.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Voted generally in favour of a higher tax rate on income over £150,000 and of a mansion tax; no statement calls for 'significantly' higher wealth taxes.

unions-good.rationale: The Commission he chaired backs the biggest strengthening of workers' rights in a generation and calls Conservative trade-union law changes unacceptable.

cut-welfare.rationale: Voted generally against cuts in welfare spending and the bedroom tax, and in 2024-25 campaigned to scrap the two-child benefit limit and review Universal Credit.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: As G20 chair in 2009 he led a pledge against protectionism and vowed to name and shame protectionist countries; told Congress protectionism 'protects no-one'; in 2025 opposed Trump's tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Commission wants a regional investment bank, an infrastructure bank mandated to cut regional inequality and place-based R&D programmes, and criticises purely free-market policy as giving up industrial policy.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: As PM he cut VAT temporarily and pressed the G20 for coordinated fiscal stimulus in 2008-09; in 2022 his Commission condemned the return of austerity.

central-bank-independence.rationale: His first act as Chancellor in 1997 was giving the Bank of England operational independence to set interest rates under an inflation target.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: As Chancellor he introduced working tax credits, treating top-ups for low earners as negative taxation.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: As Chancellor in 1997 he set a rule to borrow only to invest plus a deficit target; these were government-set rules rather than a legal constraint.

no-bailouts.rationale: His government nationalised Northern Rock, took a majority stake in RBS and recapitalised Lloyds/HBOS; he told Congress he wanted all banks stabilised, not some.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: As PM he said a tax on financial transactions was 'worth looking at'; he backed it only as a global measure.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Chaired the 2005 G8 finance deal for 100% cancellation of debts of the poorest countries; he held that most but not all unpayable debt should be removed, conditional on governance.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Drove the 2005 package doubling aid and 100% debt relief; told Congress that 'our first duty is to help the not so wealthy' and called for schooling for every child.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for IMF and World Bank reform and as G20 chair secured $100bn for development-bank lending to poor countries, but did not frame it as restructuring rules in developing countries' favour.

free-trade.rationale: Told Congress trade should again be 'the engine of prosperity', chaired the G20 anti-protectionism pledge, but adds that markets should be 'never values-free'.

common-currency.rationale: In 2003 he restated the 'principled case' that membership of a successful single currency would benefit Britain, while deferring entry because the five tests were unmet.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Commission describes the UK market as underpinned by a social market with common minimum standards in welfare, pensions and employment rights, and rejects a race to the bottom.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted for Labour's anti-terrorism laws and ID cards and as PM said he would continue the ID card scheme; these are not statements about surveillance as such.

state-harmful.rationale: The Commission he chaired calls for 'an enabling state' and a strong role for central government in equitable resource allocation.

decide-locally.rationale: The Commission's second recommendation is a legal requirement that decisions be taken as close as meaningfully possible to the people affected; he sets 'as much autonomy as possible, as much cooperation as necessary'.

assisted-dying.rationale: In November 2024 he said he opposes legalising assisted dying and argued for a funded palliative care plan instead.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: His government passed the Equality Act 2010 requiring equal treatment in employment and in private and public services, which he defended in 2010.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Commission proposes constitutionally protected social rights and constitutional protection for devolution against ordinary majorities, but not a general bill of rights.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2010 he opposed same-sex marriage; in February 2013 he said it was timely to legalise the right to marriage; the later position is used. He did not vote on the bill.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted consistently for fewer obstacles to access to abortion.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His 2006 Britishness speech urged a national day and embracing the Union flag as part of civic patriotism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: In 2006 he rejected a narrow 'cricket test' for minorities and said the flag should be a symbol of tolerance and inclusion, not racial division.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: As PM he defended a schools bill making sex education compulsory with no faith-school opt-out, including that same-sex relationships are part of life.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Called discrimination against transgender people unacceptable and pointed to the Gender Recognition Act and Equalities Bill as action.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Repeatedly called for stronger UN, IMF and World Bank powers (IMF as a 'world central bank'); as G20 chair added $500bn to IMF lending; in 2025 defended the UN and WHO.

nation-first.rationale: Says 'global problems need global solutions', chaired the 2009 G20 coordination, and argues for cooperation on 'enlightened self-interest'.

force-without-un.rationale: Voted for the 2003 Iraq war, which lacked a fresh Security Council resolution, and in 2010 called it the right decision; whether it was lawful is contested.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: As PM he signed the Lisbon Treaty and argued it needed no referendum; voted generally for more EU integration; in 2025 urged closer EU ties.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: As PM he said no one would separate Britain from the United States; in 2022 he urged NATO unity and a show of strength.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Backed the US alliance as PM and in 2022 called for NATO strength and unity against Putin.

collective-defense.rationale: In 2022 he called for NATO unity and for NATO to make clear it will not accept Russian incursions.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Voted Aye in 2007 to maintain Trident beyond the existing system and as PM refused to abandon it.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: As PM kept Trident and tied any cut to multilateral progress, saying warheads could go lower only consistent with deterrence and multilateral talks.

arms-reduction.rationale: In 2009 he urged drastic US-Russian cuts and said Britain would cut warheads or Trident tubes (12 not 16) consistent with national deterrence.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: In 2022-23 he argued for a special tribunal to prosecute Putin and his underlings for the crime of aggression.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Voted for the 2003 Iraq war and defended it at the Chilcot inquiry as the right decision; Iraq was not a response to an attack on Britain.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: As PM he made Britain a world leader on carbon cuts, urged a historic Copenhagen deal and a low-carbon recovery; his government passed the Climate Change Act; the 2022 Commission backs Net Zero.

limit-growth.rationale: The Commission he chaired says the economy needs a 'massive increase' in its growth rate and seeks prosperity in every region.

expand-nuclear.rationale: As PM in 2007 he said energy security is best safeguarded by building a new generation of nuclear stations; his government approved new build.

direct-votes.rationale: He promised then declined a referendum on the EU constitution/Lisbon, but proposed an AV referendum and, in 2010, Lords referendums.

right-to-secede.rationale: He campaigned against Scottish independence in 2014 and the Commission calls devolution permanent, but he accepted referendums as the way for Scots to decide.

proportional-representation.rationale: His 2010 reform plan was a referendum on the Alternative Vote, which is not proportional, and the Commission proposes no PR for the Commons.

separated-powers.rationale: The Commission wants a second chamber to enforce constitutional limits on government and shared power with devolved legislatures; as PM he moved some prerogative powers to Parliament.

second-chamber.rationale: The Commission he chaired proposes replacing the Lords with a smaller, democratic Assembly of the Nations and Regions alongside the Commons.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Voted generally for removing hereditary peers from the Lords; the Commission calls the unelected Lords 'indefensible'. No statement addresses titles beyond the Lords.

parliament-supreme.rationale: As PM he proposed moving the power to declare war and key appointments from the Crown to Parliament; the Commission keeps Commons primacy but wants constitutional entrenchment.

head-commands-forces.rationale: As PM he proposed shifting war-making power from the executive to Parliament.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Commission proposes constitutionally protected rights and protection of devolution so that a Commons majority cannot override them.

citizens-assembly.rationale: As PM he proposed giving citizens the right to form citizens' juries; no recorded view on randomly selected assemblies deciding policy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Commission recommends 'double devolution' giving communities a right to more say over services and places.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Commission backs restoring and strengthening devolution in Northern Ireland consistent with consent and the Good Friday Agreement.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The Commission says devolved self-government must be permanent, constitutionally protected and shielded by the second chamber from Westminster override.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The Commission commits to pooling and sharing resources across the UK to meet needs where they exist, while giving local government more revenue powers.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Commission says Whitehall has obstructed freedom of information, wants Parliament to oversee the Information Commissioner and FOI extended to private firms on public contracts.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Commission seeks to free politics from excessive influence of wealthy donors and foreign money; this concerns donors, not corporate lobbying as such.

notes: Living (born 20 February 1951). Changes of view: same-sex marriage (opposed in 2010, supported in 2013; later used). Answers rest on the 2022 Commission report he chaired, his own speeches and statements, and his government's and Commons record; news pages are cited for statements they report. Seven Ways to Change the World, My Scotland, Our Britain and Beyond the Crash were not available as full text, and Hansard budget and PMQs texts other than the 2003 euro statement could not be fetched. Many statements, notably on religion, family, culture and revolutionary ideology, are null for lack of a stated position.
